sections.title: v1.0
sections.intro: The framework you can build on today.

items.title: Records, enums, typed errors, objects
items.text: Every public type comes from the schema and arrives in each language as that language would write it.

items.title: Stores, signals, computeds, keyed lists
items.text: Reactive state in the core; list changes cross as O(change) patches.

items.title: Ten ports with adapters and fakes
items.text: Http, Kv, SecureStore, Fs, Clock, Rng, Log, Timer, Connectivity and Lifecycle, with platform adapters and deterministic Rust fakes.

items.title: Queries and mutations
items.text: Staleness, dedup, retry, optimistic rollback, an offline queue and persistence.

items.title: Streams and cancellation
items.text: Streams with backpressure; cancelling a call drops its future.

items.title: Snapshot and restore
items.text: Stores snapshot for crash recovery.

items.title: Schema-hash gate
items.text: Checked at load and at build; a mismatched UI and core refuse to talk.

items.title: undra dev
items.text: A live core over a WebSocket, rebuilt on save.

items.title: Teaching diagnostics
items.text: Every macro error says what, why and how to fix it.

items.title: 18 contract scenarios on 3 platforms
items.text: The same wire-level scenarios run against the real core on Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript: 54 of 54 pass.

items.title: Adversarial reviews of every core crate
items.text: Signals, runtime, macros and ffi were each reviewed by someone who did not write them.

sections.title: Since v1.0
sections.intro: Landed in the day after v1.0, each behind an ADR and an adversarial review.

items.title: Frame-coalesced delivery (ADR-031)
items.text: The platform mirrors merge queued change-set entries once per frame, bound their backlog and re-observe on overflow; keyed-list firehoses cost ~10x less per frame on the web. Contract scenario S18 proves a 1,000-transaction burst applies in one drain on all three platforms.

items.title: Harsh-conditions benchmark suite and the live stress screen
items.text: Firehose, event firehose, keyed churn, fan-out, stream backpressure, concurrent completions and a soak, with CI budgets that pass on the GitHub runner; the playground's stress screen shows the same numbers live in your browser.

items.title: Swift error channel (ADR-032)
items.text: Generated Swift never traps: calls throw the method's own error, CancellationError or UndraCallError; commands report through onError.

items.title: A schema loader that survives dead-stripping (ADR-029)
items.text: The loaded host core keeps its schema and JNI exports whatever else touched the target directory.

items.title: The name (ADR-030) and the wire magic (ADR-033)
items.text: Keel became Undra before anything was published; the envelope's magic bytes read UNDR.

items.title: Measured on devices
items.text: The benchmark rows come from the playground's bench hooks on the iPhone simulator, the Android emulator and Chromium, labelled as such; real-device rows the moment hardware is attached.

items.title: Android remote mode and auto-reconnect (ADR-051)
items.text: The Kotlin runtime has the WebSocket transport; all three runtimes reconnect with backoff and resume a session after a rebuild, with the status visible in the app.

items.title: Every macro error teaches
items.text: 44 codes, each with what, why, fix and a link, each with a compile-fail test; the error-codes page regenerates from the catalogue.

items.title: The whole schema in undra_schema_json (ADR-050)
items.text: The dlopen route keeps doc comments, and the Swift Port types are public, so custom ports need no fallback.

items.title: One error channel on every platform (ADR-032)
items.text: Kotlin and TypeScript calls fail with the same closed UndraCallError set as Swift; commands report instead of throwing; a lost connection is state, not an error event.

items.title: No manual build step
items.text: A Gradle task, an Xcode build phase and a Vite plugin run undra build; undra init emits CI; undra upgrade moves a project in lockstep; undra doctor names every fix.

items.title: The web bundle under its budget (ADR-052)
items.text: The hello-world core ships at 102.7 KB gzipped against a 120 KB budget, measured and gated in CI; the number on this site comes from the record.

items.title: State-preserving reload (ADR-053)
items.text: undra dev snapshots the old core and restores into the rebuilt one; the dev bar says whether the state was kept, and why not when it was not.

items.title: Derived keyed lists (ADR-039)
items.text: A filtered, sorted view over a 10,000-row list costs what changed: one row edit is 158 bytes on the wire where it was 353 KB.

items.title: Devtools (ADR-054)
items.text: A page served by undra dev: live stores, a change-set timeline with time travel, port and query logs, counters; behind a per-run token.

items.title: Persisted-state migrations and typed storage (ADR-037, ADR-049)
items.text: A changed schema still restores what the last version stored; storage ports fail with typed errors on every platform; a crashed web core restarts from its last snapshot.

items.title: A testing kit for apps (ADR-055)
items.text: Previews run the real core in process with scripted ports and a manual clock; a session recorded once with undra dev --record replays deterministically in tests on every platform.

items.title: WebSocket, SSE and Db ports (ADR-047, ADR-048)
items.text: Real-time streams with the core's credit as backpressure, and SQL over SQLite on every platform with the same deterministic fake; opt-in, so nothing grows for apps that do not use them.

items.title: Objects as parameters, host callbacks (ADR-040, ADR-041)
items.text: Generated classes cross the boundary as themselves, one wrapper per handle; the core calls back into app code through typed callback interfaces that never unwind into it.

items.title: Production operations (ADR-046)
items.text: Every contained panic becomes a structured report the app receives with symbolicable frames; background runs drain the queue under a deadline; release builds keep symbols beside the binary and undra symbolicate reads them.

sections.title: v1.x
sections.intro: In flight for the v1.x releases.

items.title: Distribution
items.text: brew, npm, a curl installer and cargo-from-git. The release pipeline is built, security-reviewed and proved by a green dry run; the three package channels go live with the v1.0.0 tag.

items.title: A runtime ends when its owner lets go (ADR-034)
items.text: Tasks hold a WeakCtx; off-core writes are refused in every build (ADR-035); a panicking computed poisons only itself; stream errors are typed on the wire (ADR-036).

items.title: Real Android adapters
items.text: Kv, SecureStore, Fs, Http, Connectivity and Lifecycle backed by the platform, installed with one call.

items.title: React Native (ADR-038)
items.text: @undra/react-native: a TurboModule over the C ABI under the same TypeScript mirror, for teams that keep React Native for the UI.

sections.title: v1.1 and v1.2
sections.intro: Planned for the releases after v1.0. The order may change with what the benchmarks show.

items.title: crates.io and Maven Central
items.text: Publish the crates under a registry-safe prefix (its own ADR) and the Kotlin runtime without a local build.

items.title: Windows CLI
items.text: Release binaries and docs for the undra command on Windows.

items.title: Migration guides
items.text: From Kotlin Multiplatform and from UniFFI; a production-shaped sample beyond the playground.

items.title: A custom domain
items.text: A home for the site and docs that is ours.

items.title: Flutter and Dart
items.text: Decided after React Native ships.

items.title: Newtypes, generics, Decimal; paged and lazy lists; polling (ADR-042, ADR-043)
items.text: In flight.

items.title: Desktop targets
items.text: macOS, Windows and Linux over the same C ABI.

items.title: A first-party inspector
items.text: Time-travel over change-sets; the wire makes it natural.

items.title: A sync engine
items.text: A separate package, not part of the core.

items.title: Compose Multiplatform interop
items.text: Use an Undra core under a Compose Multiplatform UI.

notPlanned.title: Not planned
notPlanned.text: Shared UI of any kind, and hosted services. Undra owns everything under the pixels and leaves the screens to SwiftUI, Compose and React.
